findings.title: listProposalsForTurns is fake-covered: an always-empty map survives, so the transcript's proposal cards and the snapshot's proposalSummaries are asserted nowhere
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent and not an unexecuted branch. getConversationForOwner calls listProposalsForTurns on every transcript read (reads.ts:199) with a non-empty turnIds list in this test, and context.ts readRecentTurns calls it again for the snapshot (context.ts:288). The mutant returns an empty Map before issuing the statement, so (a) every OwnerConversationTurn.proposals becomes [], which the module's own docblock (reads.ts:113-119) says cannot be substituted by summary.pendingProposals because that list is pending-only and a superseded card still belongs to the sentence that proposed it; a stored `proposal` segment carries only an id, so the card it names simply vanishes from the transcript; and (b) SnapshotTurn.proposalSummaries goes back to [] — which is EXACTLY the pre-fix behaviour this commit changed (the round-1 tree hard-coded `proposalSummaries: []`). Searched for an oracle and found none: `rg proposalSummaries src worker` returns only the two production sites and no test; `rg '\.proposals\b' across the operator and route test suites returns one hit, turn-get-route.test.ts:71, which runs behind `vi.mock('@/lib/agents/operator/reads')` and therefore asserts the route's passthrough of a fixture. reads.integration.test.ts exercises the function but asserts only conversation ids, turn ids, sequences and ownerText. The sibling singular read (listProposalsForTurn, reached through getTurnForOwner) is unasserted in exactly the same way.
findings.reason: Round 3 re-ran the always-empty-Map mutant (proposals.ts:237, `length >= 0` short-circuit) against the two live-DB cases the fix added. KILLED in both: reads.integration.test.ts:406 fails on the per-turn `toEqual` over id/operation/status; snapshot.integration.test.ts:291 fails on `proposalSummaries` (expected [] to deeply equal [ ...(2) ]), which is exactly the pre-fix behaviour. A second mutation on each row also dies: dropping the batched read's `account_id` predicate (proposals.ts:244) is caught by the foreign-account row, and forcing `describe` to the stored rationale (proposals.ts:205) is caught by the catalog sentences.

findings.title: projectOperatingRules' locationOverrideExists has no non-mocked oracle: forcing it to `true` on a location with no override row survives
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent on this fixture and not an unexecuted branch. projectOperatingRules is the single owner of the inheritance projection introduced by this commit and runs on every call of both consumers — getConversationForOwner (reads.ts:257) and buildSnapshot (context.ts:356). The seeded tenant has no auto_approval_policies row for its location, so `override.exists` is false and the mutant reports the opposite. Per the function's own docblock, locationOverrideExists is row EXISTENCE and a distinct fact from inheritance: spec §4 says a dial-only change on a location with no row CREATES one, and the card must say so — so the mutant makes the owner-facing card, and the snapshot the model reasons from, state the reverse. Searched for an oracle: the only assertion on this field anywhere is conversation-route.test.ts:64, and that suite replaces '@/lib/agents/operator/reads' wholesale (line 19 of the retargeted mock), so the `false` it asserts is the fixture it set at line 47 — the same mock-driven shape round 1 flagged as F3/F4. The only live-DB assertion on the rules object is `vetoWindowMinutes > 0` (reads.integration.test.ts:261), which is why this survived; see finding R4.
findings.reason: Round 3 re-ran the forced-`true` mutant (context.ts:102). KILLED in both live cases the fix added - reads.integration.test.ts:363 and snapshot.integration.test.ts:352 each fail `expected true to be false` on the location with no override row. A second mutation, the location projection ignoring its own effective dials and reporting the account default (context.ts:97), is also killed in both (expected 15 to be 30; { threshold: null } to deeply equal { threshold: 5 }).

findings.title: Fragile assertion: `expect(summary.rules.vetoWindowMinutes).toBeGreaterThan(0)` is a range-shaped proxy for 'the panel reports this location's effective rules' — it is what let R2 survive

Behavioural replacement: seed an auto_approval_policies row for the turn's location whose dials DIFFER from the account default, then assert equality — `summary.rules` deep-equals the location's effective threshold, vetoWindowMinutes and dailyCap, and `summary.rules.locationOverrideExists` is true; add a second location with no row and assert it inherits the account default with locationOverrideExists false. That kills R2's mutant and pins the documented 'effective, never override' rule at the same time.

Zero other siblings found.

findings.title: The R9 go-live entry the round-2 fix added misstates two of the six terminal paths it enumerates: operator_disabled emits logger.log, not logger.warn, and the lost-lease path resolves nothing
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Re-resolved against head d21db9ecd. The sentence is a universal claim over an enumerated six: 'Every terminal path in AgentTurnWorker - operator_disabled, predecessor_stalled, unauthorized (both arms), model_output_invalid, budget_exceeded, and a lease lost before completion - resolves the turn and emits a logger.warn line.' Two counterexamples in the file it describes. (a) AgentTurnWorker.ts:46 emits logger.log('agent_turn flag-off skip') - info, not warn - before failTurnAndCompleteOutbox, so a warn-level rule built from this list would not see the very path the entry singles out as 'an orderly flag-off skip'. (b) AgentTurnWorker.ts:265 warns 'agent_turn lease lost before completion' and RETURNS without resolving anything: the code's own comment says the owning attempt completes the turn and the outbox row, so it is neither terminal for the turn nor a path to page on. P1, not P0: the conclusion the entry supports - no Sentry signal anywhere in the lane, no rule row in beta-launch-alerting.md, therefore ONE go-live decision - is true and was independently re-verified this pass; what is false is the per-path detail the rule would be built from. Replacement: say the paths resolve the turn and emit a structured warning EXCEPT the flag-off skip (info) and the lost-lease exit (which resolves nothing), or drop those two from the list.
